superseded_by.reason: Residual compulsory burden must not fall on wages/salaries/ordinary earned income; active residual instrument is Residual Wealth Contribution

central_question: If Constitutional Capitalism succeeds at producing $X billion from other engines, how high can we push the income-tax starting point?

philosophy.name: Residual Progressive Income Tax
philosophy.role: Shock absorber — last revenue source activated after other public-income engines
philosophy.activation_order: Prosperity revenues first → residual gap calculated → tax begins at highest income tier → marginal rates at the top → lower-income tiers exempt → taxable boundary moves downward only if remaining gap cannot otherwise be financed
philosophy.core_question: How little ordinary earned income can we tax while still balancing the system?
philosophy.self_retiring_formula: required obligations − Use/Impact/Depletion − Value Capture/Enterprise − Human-capital − External Income − Prosperity Fund distributions = Residual Revenue Requirement; IIT schedule calibrated only to that remainder
philosophy.hard_protection: No expansion into the protected labor-income band without an explicit public trigger, published revenue shortfall, and statutory or voter-approved authorization
philosophy.marginal_not_cliff: If threshold is T, only income above T is taxed at the residual rate — earning one more dollar must not reduce after-tax income

labor_vs_rent_hierarchy_hypothesis.status: HYPOTHESIS — incidence and mobility must clear before endorsement

current_system.legal_base: Ark. Code § 26-51-201 as amended by 2026 special session Act 2 / SB1 (top rate 3.7%)
current_system.structure_note: Graduated; top 3.7% applies broadly above modest brackets — not a residual top-down design
current_system.comparison: Current system collects ~$3.859B by taxing deep into the distribution at ~3.7%. Residual design asks how much of that can be replaced by prosperity engines so the starting point rises and ordinary labor exits the tax.

soi_bind.units_note: SOI money amounts published in thousands; converted to USD
soi_bind.finer_than_1m_split_status: NEE — IRS Historic Table 2 top band is $1M+; $2M/$5M splits not locked

1M_PLUS.reading: Top band is capital/pass-through heavy vs salaries — supports testing labor vs rent distinction, but does not yet authorize different rates

gap_3b.reading: A $3B residual still requires deep reach or high rates — prosperity engines must carry most of the $3.859B for ordinary labor to exit

volatility_notes: Top-band AGI is capital-gain and pass-through heavy → residual top-down revenue more cyclical than broad wage IIT
Recession/capital-gains drought can blow out residual requirement exactly when prosperity engines may also weaken
Self-retiring design must include reserve / Prosperity Fund buffer so residual rates do not spike into protected labor in downturns

pass_through_business_incidence.note: Partnership/S-corp income is large in top bands — residual rates can hit pass-through owners who are also employers; incidence on workers/investment requires separate microsim before endorsement

COUNTABLE_NOW_PROSPERITY_ENGINES.verdict: Unchanged — residual IIT is not a prosperity engine; other engines still $0 countable

RESIDUAL_SHOCK_ABSORBER_DESIGN.verdict: Legal/admin base exists (current IIT); residual top-down calibration is a design hypothesis

NOT_LOCKED.verdict: Do not lock illustrative $5M/$2M bands or labor/rent differentials without finer data and incidence

sequence_note: Residual IIT model inserted as transition architecture alongside engine sequence; External Income remains next prosperity-engine research pass
